summary: Gateshead's parking story is shaped by the opening of the 1,000-space Quays multi-storey car park on 29 September 2025, built for an arena scheme that has still not started, and by a council that froze most car park charges for 2026/27 because earlier rises and the Tyne Bridge and flyover works had depressed use. The Gateshead Highway flyover closed in December 2024 (briefly halting Metro to Heworth) and its demolition finished on 29 September 2026, opening the way for town-centre housing schemes. Reform UK took control of the council in May 2026 and has questioned the arena. The Newcastle and Gateshead Clean Air Zone has charged older commercial vehicles since January 2023 but not private cars. The council publishes tariffs for Charles Street, Quarryfield Road and the Heworth car parks, which have been unchanged since 2024/25.

items.text: The Quays multi-storey car park on Quays Boulevard, Gateshead Quays, opened on Monday 29 September 2025 with over 1,000 spaces, 45 large accessible spaces and 50 electric vehicle charging bays. Charges are £2.60 for up to two hours or £5.70 for a full day, paid through the PayByPhone app, with 3-month and annual season tickets available.
items.source_title: New multi-storey car park opens in Gateshead

items.text: Electric vehicle charging at The Quays multi-storey car park is priced at 66 pence per kilowatt hour, according to the report on its opening; the £23 million car park was funded by Gateshead Council's capital programme plus £2.8 million from the Government's Getting Building Fund.
items.source_title: New multi-storey car park opens in Gateshead

items.text: Zapmap lists the Gateshead Quays MSCP (Hawks Road, NE8 3AD) as an APCOA-network charging site with 19 Type 2 connectors (11 at 22kW and 8 at 7.4kW) and a listed tariff of 50p/kWh, which differs from the 50 charging bays and 66p/kWh reported at the car park's opening.
items.source_title: Gateshead Quays MSCP EV charging point, Gateshead - Zapmap

items.text: In April 2021 Gateshead Council appointed Willmott Dixon to build the £22.9 million steel-framed Quays multi-storey car park in the Baltic Quarter: 10 storeys and 1,000 spaces, with 50 EV charge points initially (room for 300 more) and a new link road through the Baltic Quarter, to support the planned Newcastle Gateshead Quays arena and conference scheme.
items.source_title: Willmott Dixon awarded £22.9m Gateshead Quays multi-storey car park

items.text: In November 2020 Gateshead Council approved a £260 million conference and events development on the NewcastleGateshead Quayside: a 12,500-seat arena, over 7,000m2 of flexible event space, two hotels, bars, restaurants and car parking, to be operated by ASM Global; the venue was then scheduled to open in late 2023.
items.source_title: Plans approved for £260m Gateshead Quays regeneration scheme in UK

items.text: On 12 March 2026 Construction News reported that a contractor for the Gateshead Quays arena (12,000 to 15,000 seats, valued at £350 million) was expected to be appointed by the end of 2026, with earthworks scheduled for 2026 after a £24 million grant announced on 9 March 2026 by North East mayor Kim McGuinness; the previously planned international conference centre has been postponed and the scheme has seen repeated delays.
items.source_title: £350m Gateshead arena job appointment due this year

items.text: Gateshead Council election, 7 May 2026: Reform UK won 38 of 66 seats (Liberal Democrats 13, Labour 12, Green 3), ending Labour control that had lasted since the council's creation in 1974; Labour leader Martin Gannon lost his seat.
items.source_title: 2026 Gateshead Council election

items.text: Reform UK chose Nick Allan as its Gateshead Council group leader (reported 15 May 2026); he named road improvements giving better access to Newcastle city centre as a priority and said the group would do a lot of listening before announcing major policies.
items.source_title: Reform selects Gateshead council leader

items.text: On 4 June 2026 the new Reform leadership of Gateshead Council (leader Nick Allan, deputy leader Fiona Pearce) questioned the viability of the proposed 12,500 to 15,000-capacity Gateshead Quayside arena, while North East mayor Kim McGuinness defended the £24 million committed in March 2026 for infrastructure and enabling works.
items.source_title: Reform casts doubt on future of Gateshead Quayside Arena

items.text: Gateshead Council's Fees and Charges 2026/27 Cabinet report (24 February 2026) proposed not increasing charges at a large section of car parks because the 2022/23 and 2023/24 increases had affected usage; it noted some car parks are under-used for reasons including work on the Tyne Bridge and the flyover, and proposed freezing prices to encourage people back to the town centre.
items.source_title: Fees and Charges 2026/27 (Report to Cabinet, 24 February 2026)

items.text: On 26 February 2026 Gateshead Council signed off its parking fee changes: most car park charges frozen, with modest rises including Queen Elizabeth Avenue short-stay parking up by 10 to 20 pence (to £2 and £3), seasonal permit increases at Cross Keys Lane, Whickham Shopping Centre and Garden Street (Oakwellgate), and second and third resident permits rising to £55 and £80 a year.
items.source_title: Council signs off rise in parking permit fees across Gateshead

items.text: Gateshead Council's proposed 2025/26 fees schedule left unchanged from 2024/25 the charges at Charles Street car park (8am to 8pm, 3-hour maximum stay: £1.70 up to 1 hour, £5.10 up to 3 hours) and Quarryfield Road car park (up to 2 hours £2.60, up to 12 hours £5.70, up to 24 hours £8.00, up to 72 hours £24.00).
items.source_title: Gateshead Council Proposed Fees and Charges 2025/26

items.text: Gateshead Council's proposed 2025/26 fees schedule lists two Heworth Metro-station car parks, both unchanged from 2024/25: Heworth North (all times, maximum stay 7 days) at £2.20 up to 4 hours, £3.00 up to 12 hours and £4.20 per 24 hours; and Heworth South (Monday to Saturday 7am to 8pm, 4-hour maximum stay) at £2.40 up to 2 hours, £4.20 up to 4 hours and £2.20 fixed on Sundays.
items.source_title: Gateshead Council Proposed Fees and Charges 2025/26

items.text: Gateshead Council closed the Gateshead Highway flyover (A167) on 13 December 2024 on safety grounds; Nexus withdrew the Metro service between Central Station and Heworth on 19 December 2024 over concerns about the Metro tunnels, and after temporary propping (27 to 29 December) the Metro service was restored on 31 December 2024.
items.source_title: Gateshead Highway Flyover - Update (Report to Cabinet, 18 March 2025)

items.text: The last span of the Gateshead Highway flyover was demolished on 29 September 2026, ending a six-month project that began in April 2026; the demolition budget rose from £18 million (plus £2.5 million from the North East Combined Authority) to £31 million, and the council envisages about 1,100 new homes on the cleared area.
items.source_title: “New Era” for Gateshead as flyover demolition completes

items.text: Gateshead Council said in June 2026 that it expects a planning application in September 2026 and a start on site in mid-2027 for Capital&Centric's redevelopment of the Grade II-listed Old Town Hall and surrounding surface car parks into 243 homes plus cafes, bars and restaurants, as part of a wider aim of 4,000 new town-centre homes.
items.source_title: Gateshead signals mid-2027 start for Capital&Centric town centre renewal

items.text: In January 2026 plans for Gateshead town centre were reported to involve redeveloping the transport interchange and potentially pedestrianising Jackson Street, and council leader Martin Gannon said he was interested in adding a railway station at the Baltic Quarter.
items.source_title: Ambitious plans unveiled to transform Gateshead town centre

items.text: The Newcastle and Gateshead Clean Air Zone began charging non-compliant taxis, buses, coaches and HGVs on 30 January 2023; charges for non-compliant vans and light goods vehicles (£12.50 a day) followed on 17 July 2023, and private cars are not charged.
items.source_title: Van and light goods vehicle owners warned about start of Newcastle CAZ charges

items.text: In the first six months after the Clean Air Zone opened (to the end of July 2023), £1,301,437 in grants was paid out and 369 older, more polluting taxis, vans and HGVs were replaced or upgraded in the Newcastle and Gateshead scheme.
items.source_title: Over £1.3m awarded as North East businesses invest in cleaner vehicles

items.text: The Tyne Bridge restoration (a Gateshead-Newcastle road link) reached its two-year milestone on 2 April 2026 with the bridge kept open to traffic and pedestrians, 1,546 repairs and 3,926 rivets replaced, bridge-deck scaffolding expected in autumn 2026, main arch work from 2027 and completion planned for the centenary in 2028.
items.source_title: Two-year milestone on Tyne Bridge reached

items.text: Overnight Tyne Bridge traffic closures (8pm to 6am) were scheduled for weekdays from 3 to 28 November 2025 while scaffolding was installed on the east footway, with pedestrians and cyclists keeping access.
items.source_title: Next stage for the Tyne Bridge restoration

items.text: Metrocentre has six car parks with almost 10,000 spaces, free during centre opening hours with no time limit in the main colour-zoned car parks, while Metro Retail Park and MetrOasis have a 4-hour limit; all hold Park Mark awards.
items.source_title: Free Parking | Metrocentre | Car Parks | Multi-Storey | Metrocentre

items.text: The BALTIC car park behind the gallery is pay on exit by card or cash at £2.00 up to 1 hour, £3.50 up to 2 hours, £5.00 up to 3 hours and £1.50 an hour thereafter, with free parking for Blue Badge holders.
items.source_title: Getting to Baltic

items.text: The Glasshouse International Centre for Music car park (NE8 2BA) is managed with Euro Car Parks using ANPR, free for up to 1 hour and £5.95 all day; the venue lists Church Street, Quarryfield Road (500m) and The Quays multi-storey (700m, 1,000+ spaces) as alternatives and notes Mill Road and South Shore Road car parks as currently closed.
items.source_title: Parking at The Glasshouse

items.text: Heworth is one of the Metro park-and-ride stations recommended for events at Gateshead International Stadium (via Gateshead Stadium Metro station), alongside Callerton Parkway, Regent Centre, Four Lane Ends, Northumberland Park and Stadium of Light; Travel North East says Metro runs at least every 12 minutes from park-and-ride stations and more frequently at peak times from Heworth.
items.source_title: How To Get There - Gateshead Half Marathon & 10k at Gateshead International Stadium

items.text: In February 2025 the North East Combined Authority, of which Gateshead Council is a partner, secured £15.8 million from the Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure fund, aiming for over 1,000 new charge points by 2030 across the region, mainly in residential areas without off-street parking.
items.source_title: £15.8m boost to North East electric charging network
